author: Robert Smith
title: Shiloh community residents claim flooding shortly after ALDOT's mitigation project - NewsBreak
text:
By Robert Smith ,
4 hours ago
ELBA, Ala. ( WDHN ) — After the State Department of Transportation wrapped up its flooding mitigation project for the Shiloh community at the end of August, residents claim about two weeks later the nightmare returned as they saw flooding after nearly 30 minutes to an hour of rain last weekend.
"It's like deja vu all over again," Shiloh resident Timothy Williams said. "That water came through and washed away the soil and it brought back memories. We said it's not a fix we asked them and FHWA (Federal Highway Administration) for a fix and pipe the water out, but they gave us ditches and it has no where to go but over back onto our property."
After ALDOT previously said property owners were not responsive to option one, they went with option 2 -- a project they believed would function as designed.
It consisted of building a new detention basin, expanding and modifying existing basins and expanding roadside ditches to mitigate the storm water.
Resident claim instead of the project mitigating water, its holding water for nearly a week which has welcomed unwanted visitors to the community such as frogs and water moccasins.
"It has caused us a nightmare out her. We have been dealing with flooding for 8 years. We shouldn't have to live like that, dealing with all these insects, snakes and frogs. They put a levee up, but it's a depreciation of our property," Williams said.
Although the project is completed, residents are asking the Federal Highway Administration to get back involved. They wrote a letter proposing five requests.
Halt formal VRA sign-off until a comprehensive independent technical audit is completed. Compel ALDOT to immediately release the complete hydrologic and hydraulic modeling files to the community and their designated experts. Require ALDOT to implement corrective structural measures to safely route stormwater away from private properties without relying on illegal restrictive covenants or destructive standing basins. Hold a joint FHWA/ALDOT public meeting on the drainage improvement project before FHWA approval. Request that independent hydraulic engineers evaluate whether ALDOT's proposed corrective measures will truly restore flood risk in the Shiloh community to pre-2017. "We want them to come out here and give us a total fix and not satisfy the VRA," Williams said. "The ALDOT guy stopped in and I was able to show him the water and the damages it caused. We just want them to come out here and do the right thing fix the problem."
We contacted ALDOT for a response, but they refused to comment.
